subject.title: [Bug]: Sandbox container exits immediately when no-new-privileges is applied (exec /usr/bin/sleep: operation not permitted)

question: Should OpenClaw support a Docker sandbox `no-new-privileges` opt-out or fallback for hosts where that Docker flag causes exec EPERM?
rationale: The issue blocks sandbox sessions on the reported host, but each meaningful recovery path either preserves the security boundary and leaves hosts blocked or weakens the sandbox boundary under operator control.

options.title: Explicit Dangerous Override
options.body: Add a documented dangerous config key with secure default true, and surface `false` in status, doctor, and security-audit output.

options.title: Diagnostic Only
options.body: Keep the flag mandatory and improve startup/status errors so operators can identify the host-level Docker incompatibility without weakening the sandbox.

options.title: Narrow EPERM Fallback
options.body: Retry without the flag only for a tightly detected startup EPERM and record the runtime as weakened for audit/status visibility.

recommendation.title: Explicit Dangerous Override
recommendation.body: Add a documented dangerous config key with secure default true, and surface `false` in status, doctor, and security-audit output.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest history signal on the current Docker sandbox module and adjacent sandbox hardening policy.
